precepts.text: I have kept the ways of the Lord and not wickedly departed from my God; I did not put away his statutes from me. When Nathan confronted David over Bathsheba and Uriah, he did not answer 'I am king'; he acknowledged his sin, accepted the judgment and walked on, a man after God's heart.
precepts.point: Forgive, lest Satan should get an advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices. Examine whether a subtle pride is his device on you: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, refusing correction. Captain Matthew adds that pride is also why a heavy brother will not change his eating.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Paul forgives “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” So examine yourself: has Satan been using some form of pride to hold you back and keep you down? It may be subtle: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, I'm good, I'm fine. Satan has many devices and can transform himself into an angel of light. Captain Matthew put it plainly: fat brothers are too prideful, and that is why they won't change their eating habits.

David shows the other way. “The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God. For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.” We all know David committed adultery and put out a hit on a brother. So what does it mean that he did not put away his statutes?

When Nathan the prophet brought it to him, he said, that's me. God was going to take away the child; he fasted and prayed, and when it happened he washed his face, ate bread and said it was the Lord's judgment. He was not prideful. He did not say, I'm the king, I can have as many women as I want, God chose me. He acknowledged his sin, humbled himself and did not put the judgments away.

“I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.” He went on forward and walked in the ways of the Lord, to the point where God said David is a man after my own heart, because he humbled himself when his sins were brought to him. That is how you keep Satan from getting an advantage of you.

precepts.text: David said, by my God have I leaped over a wall; David was a mighty man of war.
precepts.point: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
David said, “For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.” David was a mighty man of war.

So when Zechariah says “he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”, that is the strength in view: “they that stumbled are girded with strength.”

precepts.text: His feet like hinds' feet, fast like a deer, and a bow of steel broken by his arms: David bent steel, took down lions and bears, and killed a giant with a rock and a sling. He that is feeble shall be as David goes right back to they that stumbled are girded with strength; that is the house of Israel.
precepts.point: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“He maketh my feet like hinds’ feet, and setteth me upon my high places. He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.” His feet were fast like a deer, and a bow of steel was broken by his arms. David bent steel, took down lions and bears, and killed a giant with a rock and a sling.

Zechariah's word, “he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”, goes right back to Hannah's word, “they that stumbled are girded with strength.” That is the house of Israel.

In the same verses Hannah is talking about herself: “the barren hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.”

precepts.text: By thee I have run through a troop, and by my God have I leaped over a wall; David knew his power source.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
David said it himself: “For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.”

David knew his power source. That is why he enquired of the Lord before going up against the Philistines, and why he waited for the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees before he moved. It was by his God that he ran through the host of the Philistines, not by his own strength.

precepts.text: He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms; David's strength was of the Most High.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.”

David's strength was of the Most High. The Lord taught him war in the plainest way at the mulberry trees: go not up, fetch a compass behind them, and move when you hear the sound in the tree tops. David did so, “as the Lord had commanded him”, and smote the Philistines from Geba to Gazer. The hands were David's, but the Lord taught them to war.

precepts.text: It is God that girdeth me with strength, maketh my feet like hinds' feet, teacheth my hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms; that is the strength the Most High gave David in his youth.
precepts.point: These giants were tall men, one about eight or nine feet, not the twenty foot giants of fairy tales. Goliath had kin, and eventually they were all served by David and his servants.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

precepts.why:
“It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect. He maketh my feet like hinds’ feet, and setteth me upon my high places. He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.” That is the strength the Most High gave David in his youth.

Now David was getting up in age. The Philistines had war again with Israel, “and David waxed faint.” Ishbi-benob, of the sons of the giant, “thought to have slain David. But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him.” Then David’s men swore, “Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel.” It was time for him to sit on the throne.

His servants finished the work. At Gob and at Gath the sons of the giant fell: Sibbechai the Hushathite slew one, Elhanan slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite, “the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam”, and Jonathan the son of Shimea, David’s brother, slew a man of great stature “that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes”. These were tall men, one about eight or nine feet, not the twenty foot giants of fairy tales. Goliath had kin, and “These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.”

precepts.text: Among the nations we find no ease but a trembling heart, failing eyes, sorrow of mind, and life hanging in doubt with fear day and night; this includes depression that many of our people suffer, and the constant fear even a law-abiding person feels when police pull up behind them.
precepts.point: The sorrows of death describe the curses of the scattering.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of ungodly men made me afraid.” The sorrows of death describe the curses of the scattering, and Moses laid them out: “And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind”.

“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Among the nations we find no ease, but a trembling heart, failing eyes, sorrow of mind, and life hanging in doubt with fear day and night.

That includes the depression so many of our people suffer, and the constant fear even a law-abiding person feels when the police pull up behind them. Those are the sorrows of death and the sorrows of hell compassing us about, and it is in that distress that David called upon the Lord, and he heard his voice out of his temple.

precepts.text: If we disobey, they that hate us shall reign over us and we shall be slain before our enemies; this is why the wicked oppressor rules right now, and why our people run when the police come even when innocent.
precepts.point: We are still looking for that deliverance from our strong enemy and them that hate us.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David was delivered “from my strong enemy, and from them which hated me: for they were too strong for me.” Leviticus tells why they that hate us are too strong for us: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

If we disobey, they that hate us reign over us and we are slain before our enemies. That is why the wicked oppressor rules right now. And “ye shall flee when none pursueth you” is why our people run when the police come, even when they are innocent.

We are still looking for that deliverance from our strong enemy and from them that hate us, the deliverance David sings of when the Lord drew him out of many waters.

precepts.text: The large place ties to being brought into the wilderness of the people, where the Most High delivers again.
precepts.point: They prevented him in the day of his calamity, but the Lord was his stay and brought him forth into a large place because he delighted in him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“He brought me forth also into a large place; he delivered me, because he delighted in me.” That large place ties to Ezekiel: “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.”

The Most High brings us into the wilderness of the people and pleads with us face to face there. That is where he delivers again, bringing us out into a large place because he delights in us, the way he was David's stay in the day of his calamity.

precepts.text: A young man cleanses his way by taking heed according to the word.
precepts.point: We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David says the Lord recompensed him “according to the cleanness of my hands”. How do we get clean hands? “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.”

A young man cleanses his way by taking heed according to the word. We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism. That is what David means when he says he kept the ways of the Lord and did not put away his statutes from him.

precepts.text: Ye are clean through the word which Christ has spoken; the cleansing did not change in the New Testament.
precepts.point: We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Christ tells his disciples, “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” Ye are clean through the word, the same way a young man cleanses his way in Psalms 119:9.

The cleansing did not change in the New Testament. It was never water baptism; it is the word. David's clean hands, recompensed by the Lord, came from keeping the ways of the Lord and his statutes, and Christ says the same: clean through the word.

precepts.text: To the law and to the testimony; if they speak not according to this word there is no light in them, so we learn and apply the law to clean ourselves up.
precepts.point: We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” Everything is measured by the law and the testimony; whoever speaks not according to this word has no light in him.

So we learn and apply the law to clean ourselves up. That is the cleanness of hands David speaks of: “For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.” Keep the judgments and statutes before you, and you keep yourself from your iniquity, which is sin.

precepts.text: The grace of God teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts and to live soberly and righteously, so grace itself teaches us to keep the commandments.
precepts.point: We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Grace does not do away with the commandments; it teaches them. “For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world”.

The grace of God teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts and to live soberly and righteously. So grace itself teaches us to keep the commandments. That is how David was upright before the Lord and kept himself from his iniquity, and how we get clean today.

precepts.text: Mortify your members, fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness which is idolatry, for which the wrath of God comes on the disobedient.
precepts.point: David kept the Most High's judgments and statutes before him and kept himself from his iniquity. Iniquity is sin.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Keeping yourself from your iniquity means putting sin to death: “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry”.

Mortify your members: fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry. These are the things the wrath of God comes on the disobedient for.

David says, “I kept myself from mine iniquity.” Iniquity is sin, and this is the list to keep yourself from. That is the cleanness of hands the Lord recompenses.

precepts.text: He confirmed his words against us and our judges by bringing on us a great evil, not against all people but against us, as was done upon Jerusalem, who are the Israelites.
precepts.point: He will save the afflicted people but bring down high looks. Israel is the afflicted people the scripture is talking about.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“For thou wilt save the afflicted people; but wilt bring down high looks.” Israel is the afflicted people the scripture is talking about, and Daniel shows why we are the afflicted: “And he hath confirmed his words, which he spake against us, and against our judges that judged us, by bringing upon us a great evil: for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.”

He confirmed his words against us and against our judges by bringing on us a great evil. Not against all people, but against us, as was done upon Jerusalem, who are the Israelites. Nothing under the whole heaven has been done like what was done to us.

With the froward he shows himself froward, and we were froward. But he is the one who will save the afflicted people, and bring down the high looks of those over us.

precepts.text: Ye shall chase your enemies and five shall chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight; this is the power we are looking to receive.
precepts.point: As for God, his way is perfect and the word of the Lord is tried; he is a buckler to all that trust in him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.” That is the strength the Most High girds his people with, and Leviticus tells what it looks like: “And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword. And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.”

Five chase a hundred, and a hundred put ten thousand to flight. This is the power we are looking to receive. It is God that girds us with strength and makes our way perfect, and he is a buckler to all those that trust in him.

precepts.text: The remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles as a lion among the beasts, treading down and tearing in pieces with none to deliver, and every enemy shall be cut off; another proof we were scattered everywhere like the dew and rain, and a picture of the strength the Most High returns to us.
precepts.point: He enlarges David's steps under him so his feet do not slip; David pursues his enemies, overtakes them, and does not turn again till they are consumed.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“He teacheth my hands to war”, David says, and “I have pursued mine enemies, and overtaken them: neither did I turn again till they were consumed.” Micah shows the remnant of Jacob with that same strength in the last days.

“And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the Lord, as the showers upon the grass”. That is another proof we were scattered everywhere, like the dew and the rain falling on the whole earth.

Then the strength returns: “the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver.” Treading down and tearing in pieces with none to deliver is David wounding his enemies so they cannot rise, fallen under his feet.

“Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off.” Every enemy cut off: that is the Most High giving us the necks of our enemies, and it is a picture of the strength he returns to us.

precepts.text: The sons of them that afflicted us shall come bending, showing the strangers submitting themselves.
precepts.point: The Most High delivers him from the strivings of the people and makes him the head of the heathen; a people whom he has not known shall serve him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“As soon as they hear of me, they shall obey me: the strangers shall submit themselves unto me.” Isaiah shows that submission: “The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet”.

The sons of them that afflicted us come bending, and they that despised us bow down at the soles of our feet. That is the strangers submitting themselves, when the Most High makes us the head of the heathen and a people we have not known serve us.

“and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” The strangers that fade away and are afraid out of their close places are the very ones who will call us the city of the Lord.

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven suffereth violence and the violent take it by force; the violent men of that time were Rome fighting against the kingdom, which is Israel.
precepts.point: He delivers David from his enemies and lifts him above those that rise against him, delivering him from the violent man. The enemies are not just going to and fro; there is a people who serve satan, the so-called white man, to make it plain.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“thou hast delivered me from the violent man.” Christ speaks of that violence: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

The kingdom of heaven suffered violence, and the violent men of that time were Rome, fighting against the kingdom, which is Israel. The enemies are not just going to and fro; there is a people who serve satan, the so-called white man, to make it plain. Those are the violent that David is delivered from when the Most High lifts him up above those that rise up against him.

precepts.text: The Most High chose Solomon to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel, so the kingdom of God is Israel.
precepts.point: He delivers David from his enemies and lifts him above those that rise against him, delivering him from the violent man. The enemies are not just going to and fro; there is a people who serve satan, the so-called white man, to make it plain.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
The kingdom the violent take by force is Israel. David says: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.”

The Most High chose Solomon to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel. So the kingdom of God is Israel. When the kingdom of heaven suffers violence in Matthew 11:12, it is Israel suffering the violent man, and it is God that avenges David and subdues the people under him.

precepts.text: This great deliverance is the good news, for a remnant of Israel is fighting for our enemies and against the remnant of Jacob, but the righteous will be accepted.
precepts.point: Great deliverance he gives to his king and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Great deliverance giveth he to his king”. This great deliverance is the good news: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.”

A remnant of Israel is fighting for our enemies and against the remnant of Jacob, but the righteous will be accepted. The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies go together, and that is why David gives thanks among the heathen and sings praises to his name.

precepts.text: The days come that it shall no more be said the Lord liveth that brought Israel out of Egypt, but the Lord liveth that brought the children of Israel from the land of the north, which is North America, and from all the lands whither he had driven them; if the people in the land now were not Israel, why are they still here in New York, Hollywood, and Miami.
precepts.point: Great deliverance he gives to his king and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
The great deliverance and mercy shown to David's seed for evermore is spelled out in Jeremiah: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them”.

The land of the north is North America. He brings the children of Israel from there and from all the lands where he drove them, “and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.”

If the people in the land now were not Israel, why are they still here in New York, Hollywood, and Miami? The Most High put us here, and it is he who brings us back, the deliverance he gives to his king and his seed for evermore.

points: For thou wilt light my candle. You see that? David said, you are going to light my candle. That is that spirit. How do you think Solomon got that information? His father knew it. He said, you are going to light my candle.
The Lord my God will enlighten my darkness. He said he is going to enlighten the darkness.

note.label: Ignite Your Influence

points: For by thee I have run through a troop. He said, now I am able to run through a troop. I am able to run through ten thousand. Think about the strength David had. He said, when you enlighten my spirit, I was running through a troop.

And by my God have I leaped over a wall. I am leaping over walls. Imagine you are seeing your leader, King David, running through a troop, leaping over a wall. It is going to make you do the same thing. You are going to be like, I am leaping over walls too. I am igniting.

The bishop did a class, a very good class, on a sheep leading lions versus a lion leading sheep. You get one lion leading a flock of sheep, they will forget that they are sheep in the face of fear. But if a sheep leads a pack of lions, they question the fierceness within them. This is what David is saying. When his spirit got enlightened, he was able to run through a troop, leap over walls.

points: As for God, his way is perfect: the word of the Lord is tried: he is a buckler to all those that trust in him. A buckler is a covering for everybody that trusts in him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: The Most High lights David's candle and enlightens his darkness; by his God he has run through a troop and leaped over a wall.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: As for God, his way is perfect and the word of the Lord is tried; he is a buckler to all that trust in him.
There is no God save the Lord and no rock save our God. It is God that girds David with strength, makes his way perfect, and makes his feet like hinds' feet.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: He teaches David's hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms; he gives him the shield of his salvation, his right hand holds him up, and his gentleness makes him great.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: He enlarges David's steps under him so his feet do not slip; David pursues his enemies, overtakes them, and does not turn again till they are consumed.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: David wounds his enemies so they cannot rise; they fall under his feet, for the Most High girded him with strength for the battle and subdued under him those that rose up against him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: His enemies cry but there is none to save them, even unto the Lord, but he answers them not; David beats them small as the dust before the wind and casts them out as dirt in the streets.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: The Most High delivers him from the strivings of the people and makes him the head of the heathen; a people whom he has not known shall serve him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: As soon as they hear of him the strangers submit and fade away, afraid out of their close places.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: The Lord liveth, blessed be his rock, and let the God of his salvation be exalted; it is God that avenges David and subdues the people under him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: He delivers David from his enemies and lifts him above those that rise against him, delivering him from the violent man. The enemies are not just going to and fro; there is a people who serve satan, the so-called white man, to make it plain.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: Therefore David gives thanks among the heathen and sings praises to the Most High's name.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

points: Great deliverance he gives to his king and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed forevermore.
